-59.54000,13.19000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
-59.54000,13.19000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-87.20400,30.46740.name: New Leaders in Fertility & Endocrinology, LLC
-87.20400,30.46740.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Barry A. Ripps, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-121.27360,38.13428.name: AgBio Company
-121.27360,38.13428.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-106.62630,52.13734.name: Vaccine and Infectious Disease Organization, Centre for Pandemic Research
-106.62630,52.13734.state: 120 Veterinary Road Saskatoon, SK, S7N 5E3 Canada, Canada
-106.62630,52.13734.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, planned. Run by University of Saskatchewan. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on both human and animal health. Operational or announced: Announced 2021. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-122.27270,37.87160.name: Pivot Bio — PROVEN product record
-122.27270,37.87160.desc: A nitrogen-fixing microbial product applied across millions of US acres, using engineered soil bacteria that supply nitrogen to maize directly. It is one of the largest deliberate releases of engineered microorganisms into open farmland anywhere, registered as a crop input, and it attracts almost none of the attention an engineered plant would.

-122.27270,37.87160.name: Zymergen / Ginkgo — the collapse and absorption
-122.27270,37.87160.desc: Zymergen raised heavily on automated organism engineering, listed publicly in 2021, disclosed months later that its lead product had no viable market, and was bought by Ginkgo for a fraction of its valuation. It is the clearest failure on this map, and it is here because the pitch it failed on — that engineering biology would industrialise like software — is the pitch the sector still makes.

-77.03500,38.90100.name: American Farm Bureau Federation
-77.03500,38.90100.desc: The largest US farm organisation, and a consistent supporter of agricultural biotechnology in legislative and trade fights. Farm organisations are where adoption is argued out among the people who actually plant, and their positions carry weight that no company’s does — which is also why membership organisations of this size are worth lobbying.

127.36000,36.39000.name: Korea Institute of Toxicology (KIT)
127.36000,36.39000.state: Daejeon — Daedeok Science Town, with a Jeonbuk branch
127.36000,36.39000.desc: A government-funded institute under South Korea's science ministry that assesses the safety of medicines, pesticides, food additives, cosmetics and industrial chemicals, and sells non-clinical assessment as a service. Its good laboratory practice system is certified against both OECD and US food and drug administration criteria, and it was the first organisation in Asia accredited by the international laboratory animal care body. Its predictive toxicology department works on in vitro and in silico methods intended to replace animal tests. Two things make it the right entry for this facet's last hole: a state institute competing as a contract laboratory is a different actor from the listed companies that dominate here, and a body whose income depends on animal studies is simultaneously developing the methods meant to displace them.
